statements.text: There is likely a berserk wing of the artificial intelligence community that intentionally or unintentionally could use artificial intelligence to kill all of us and hurt us the entire time that we are dying.
statements.context: Senator Kennedy poses a question to a witness during a Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI oversight.

statements.text: We ought to first pass a law that says you can use AI for these uses but not others. Is that what you're saying?
statements.context: Senate hearing on AI oversight, Senator Kennedy questioning a witness about whether AI use cases should be restricted by law.

statements.text: And so I would have funding to try to basically focus on AI safety research. That term has a lot of complications in my field.
statements.context: Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI rules where Senator Kennedy questions witness Professor Gary Marcus.

statements.text: Sensible safeguards are not in opposition to innovation. Accountability is not a burden. Far from it. They are the foundation of how we can move ahead while protecting public trust.
statements.context: Opening statement by Senator Blumenthal at a Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI oversight.

statements.text: Yes. Mr. Dally, if I am a recipient of content created by generative AI, do you think I should have a right to know that that content was generated by a robot?
statements.context: Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI oversight; Senator Kennedy questions witness Bill Dally (NVIDIA Chief Scientist) about consumer transparency for AI-generated content.

statements.text: It says if you own a robot that's going to spit out artificial content to consumers, consumers have the right to know that it was generated by a robot and who owns the robot.
statements.context: Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI oversight where Senator Kennedy reflects on legislative readiness and describes his disclosure bill.

statements.text: But as a principle, do you think that people should have a right to know when they're being fed content from generative AI?
statements.context: Senate hearing titled 'Oversight of A.I.: Legislating on Artificial Intelligence', with Senator Kennedy questioning a witness.

statements.text: Professor, do you think the consumer should be able to know not only that the content is generated by AI, but do you think this consumer is entitled to know who owns the robot and therefore the generated content?
statements.context: Senate hearing on Artificial Intelligence in Financial Services, where Senator Kennedy questions an expert witness.

statements.text: Do you think AI can improve on that in terms of determining precisely who is likely to pay the loan back and who is not?
statements.context: Senate hearing on Artificial Intelligence in Financial Services, questioning a witness about AI in loan underwriting.

statements.text: As a matter of fact, just last week a report from the Department of Homeland Security warned, and I will quote, ``As the 2024 election cycle progresses, generative AI tools likely provide both domestic and foreign threat actors with enhanced opportunities for interference by aggravating emergent events, disrupting election processes, or attacking election infrastructure.''
statements.context: House Homeland Security Committee hearing on AI and homeland defense, held during the 2024 election cycle.

statements.text: But how can we better harness the institutes of higher ed, especially our public institutions, for getting at this cutting-edge technology? While they are training up our youth in this new technology how do we make sure that they are developing it in a safe way regarding AI?
statements.context: House Homeland Security Committee hearing on harnessing AI to secure the homeland.

statements.text: You don't know whether the advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence chips are prohibited from being sold to China?
statements.context: Senate hearing on national security through export controls, investment security, and the Defense Production Act.

statements.text: Mr. Speaker, I rise to celebrate Dr. Venu Govindaraju as Person of the Year by the Council of Heritage and Arts of India. [...] Mr. Speaker, please join me in celebrating Dr. Venu Govindaraju as Person of the Year by the Council of Heritage and Arts of India.
statements.context: A US House floor tribute speech honoring Dr. Venu Govindaraju as Person of the Year by the Council of Heritage and Arts of India.
